```{r,echo=FALSE}

cn = function(real,imag){
    ss = paste0("{",real,"}+",imag,"i")
    ss = gsub("+-","-",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("+1i","+i",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("-1i","-i",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("+0i","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{0}+","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{0}-","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("}","",ss,fixed=T)
    return(ss)
}

rm = sample(2:9,2)*sample(c(-1,1),2,T)

R = rm[1]
M = rm[2]

cn1 = cn(R,M)
cn2 = cn(R,-M)

ach1 = paste0("(x+",-R,"+",-M,"i)(x+",-R,"+",M,"i)",collapse = "")
ach2 = paste0("(x+",R,"+",-M,"i)(x+",R,"+",M,"i)",collapse = "")
ach3 = paste0("(x+",-R,"+",M,"i)(x+",R,"+",M,"i)",collapse = "")
ach4 = paste0("(x+",-R,"+",-M,"i)(x+",R,"+",-M,"i)",collapse = "")

ach1 = gsub("+-","-",ach1,fixed=T)
ach2 = gsub("+-","-",ach2,fixed=T)
ach3 = gsub("+-","-",ach3,fixed=T)
ach4 = gsub("+-","-",ach4,fixed=T)

ach = sample(c(ach1,ach2,ach3,ach4))
al = paste0("* $",ach,"$",collapse="\n")
sol = paste0(1*(ach1==ach),collapse="")

ff = paste0("(x-(",R,"+",M,"i))(x-(",R,"+",-M,"i))",collapse = "")
ff = gsub("+-","-",ff,fixed=T)

```

Question
========

Which of the quadratic polynomials below has a root of $`r cn1`$ and real coefficients (when in standard expanded form)?

Answerlist
--------

`r al`

Solution
========

The correct answer is $`r ach1`$.

If the polynomial has real coefficients, then the other root must be $`r cn2`$. We can then express each factor as $x$ minus the root.

$$`r ff`$$

Distribute the subtraction across the parentheses to get the correct answer.

$$`r ach1`$$

Notice that $`r ach4`$ has $`r cn1`$ as a root, but if you expand it, there will be imaginary/complex coefficients.
